Description: Find a song on external services — play, stream, search or buy (links to YouTube, Bandcamp, stores)
Play the song in the linked Apple Music app (AppleScript bridge, local only)
Filter songs by year while browsing
Filter by key
Filter by owned vs streaming (cloud) files
Browse a DJ-specific subset of the library (e.g. owned files, DJ tags) that matches a rekordbox USB stick for playing on decks
Define minimum metadata standards (required fields, required tags based on other tags) and surface songs that fall short, with easy ways to fix them
Consistent metadata for tracks with multiple artists (split, detect, keep consistent when saved)
Store featured/remix artists separately (featuredArtists), so finding songs by an artist includes ft./remix credits, with control to hide or separate them
Apply style tags or other metadata from one track to multiple other tracks (e.g. copy/paste)
Normalise tags on entry — control how grouped tags split (e.g. 'Deep House' → 'Deep'), not just split-on-space
Find similar or synonymous tags and rationalise them (e.g. DeepHouse → Deep House, Hip-Hop/Rap → Hip Hop) to reduce synonyms
Import and store playlists (shows), e.g. from CSV or text
Create a playlist or set (e.g. radio show, theme mix) — find songs, add individually or in bulk, arrange them
Share a playlist or show — pastable formatted tracklist, tracklist image, cover art, or a rich embeddable HTML tracklist
Backup library / database
Automated scheduled import from Apple Music (e.g. cron job export ⇒ import daily)
Sync favourite / starred / heart state quickly and easily from Apple Music
Write metadata back to Apple Music safely and reliably (pass argv, not interpolated AppleScript — no escaping/quoting bugs)
Import reports favourite sync accurately (Un-starred count not always 0)
Robust, accurate UI for syncing edited metadata back to Apple Music (e.g. 'Saved to Apple Music' stays stale after edits, 'no changes to save' misdetected, silent save failures)
Robust bulk write or resync of metadata to Apple Music without editing first (e.g. push imported key/tempo back; incremental, resumable sync-back larger than one page)
Track edits that still need syncing back to Apple Music, and apply them all
Clean URLs — no redundant duplication (e.g. artist page URL where the same artist appears in both path and query string)
Enter BPM (tempo) easily without fighting the number field
Consistent capitalisation for labels/styles (auto-capitalise on edit/import/normalise)
Freeze a CrateCaddy query as a regular Apple Music playlist (e.g. gig prep, running, work)
One validated write pathway (single source of truth) — history, validation, normalisation always applied via an ORM/normalisation layer
Remove or archive tracks that are no longer in Apple Music (keep the library tidy)
Clear audit trail of all writes and edits
Search the library — one text field with a results page (simple search)
Allow exact tag matching as an option (e.g. 'House' matches only 'House', not 'Deep House')
Edit history UI clearly shows what has changed (edited fields, tags as added/removed)
Handle duplicate versions of a song — detect them, show all versions, keep the one you want (e.g. purchased)
Consistent, robust musical key handling — import keeps any valid key (flats not dropped), normalise to sharps and Camelot
Multi-user, anywhere access — cloud database with replication and events, user auth, feeding static + local clients
Pull cover art from Apple Music so songs are visually identifiable while browsing
Consistent render order for Grouping and Genres, normalised on save-back to Apple Music (e.g. DJing before Listening)
Ensure the filter bar works well on small screens
Touch-friendly tempo range filter
Support OR genre tag filtering in the UI, equal status to AND (currently AND-first, OR only via URL syntax)
Indicate in genre cloud which tags are included/excluded with an affordance (such as green/red highlight or shading)
Maximise ability to view the song list, especially on small screens
Helpful text hints when no songs found - e.g. explain current tag filter
Song page: Show related, similar or suggested songs to play next (with hints such as nearby tempo and key)
Consolidate scattered hardcoded colours and sizes into CSS design tokens (shared theming layer)
